data.exact_reserve_text: During the year, the Syndicate released GBP 9.8m of technical reserves in respect of prior years (2021: GBP 9.6m) arising from the nuclear property and nuclear liability classes (2021: from the nuclear property and nuclear liability classes).

named_events.loss_description: Since the nuclear industry's formation in the early 1950s there has only been one significant core melt nuclear event paid by the insurance market, at Three Mile Island in the US in 1979.
Following the Fukushima accident in March 2011, an extensive review of the Syndicate's potential catastrophe exposure was undertaken, and exposure is considered to be limited.

The largest insured windstorm loss to date was from a spares warehouse on a nuclear site from Hurricane Andrew in 1992. While the warehouse was damaged, with losses in the region of $200m, there was no damage to the nuclear unit.

named_events.event_name: Ukraine conflict / sanctions on Russia (exposure note)
named_events.loss_description: The Syndicate has no further involvement in the small exposure it had to Russian risks, following international sanctions introduced. It does maintain a small exposure in Ukraine for some liability policies, but there is an appropriate war exclusion clause in place.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate recorded a prior-year release of GBP 9.8m in 2022 (approximately 26.1% of opening gross claims outstanding), arising from nuclear property and nuclear liability business. The release was driven by favourable claims development and settlements being below previous reserves, consistent with the underwriting commentary that few claims were notified and those settled below reserve expectations.
raw_causal_phrases: During the year, the Syndicate released GBP 9.8m of technical reserves in respect of prior years (2021: GBP 9.6m) arising from the nuclear property and nuclear liability classes (2021: from the nuclear property and nuclear liability classes).
We have received very few claims and those we did receive were settled at less than reserved. The total property losses advised to date are within forecast loss expectancy.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development taken from Note 4 narrative which explicitly states a GBP 9.8m release. Opening gross claims outstanding taken from Note 15 reconciliation (gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2022). No LOB-level split of the GBP 9.8m release is provided, so LOB allocation is inferred (nuclear property and liability statements). Claims development triangle is present and included as an auxiliary source but RITC effects and aggregated 'and prior' column limit precise triangle-based PYD computation.
